OpenAI says GPT-6 Cyber helped validate 948 Linux kernel bugs in one run. Patches went to humans for review.

Then they open-sourced Shirudo, a runtime that lets agents shield systems from exploits without downtime.

Agents found the bugs. People reviewed the fixes.

That's the pattern I want for every agent in the enterprise.

hits.original:

hits.draft_en:
ChatGPT just gave GPT-5.6 a retirement date: December 23.

Good reminder for anyone building agents. If your agent, flow or prompt only works on one specific model, you've built in an expiry date.

Test on the next model before the old one sunsets. Write instructions that survive a model swap.

Models retire. Your agent shouldn't.
hits.video_tip: Vertical 8s: a sticky note on your monitor reading 'GPT-5.6' gets peeled off and replaced with a blank one, you shrug and keep typing. Caption: 'Build for the swap.'

drafts.rides: @ChatGPT GPT-5.6 deprecation Dec 23 (1.74M) + @ChatGPT GPT-6.2 Sol in Chat (1.26M) + @github Copilot Fusion routing (80K)
drafts.text:
ChatGPT just gave GPT-5.6 a retirement date: December 23.

Good reminder for anyone building agents. If your agent, flow or prompt only works on one specific model, you've built in an expiry date.

Test on the next model before the old one sunsets. Write instructions that survive a model swap.

Models retire. Your agent shouldn't.
drafts.video_tip: Vertical 8s: a sticky note on your monitor reading 'GPT-5.6' gets peeled off and replaced with a blank one, you shrug and keep typing. Caption: 'Build for the swap.'

drafts.rides: @satyanadella "Outcome per dollar is the frontier" (176K) + @MicrosoftAI Rocket RL infra (402K) + @burkeholland MAI Code 2 at 5% of the cost (25K)
drafts.text:
Satya Nadella: outcome per dollar is the frontier.

Burke Holland says MAI Code 2 hits 96% of Opus 5.5's performance at 5% of the cost.

That's the agent question in Copilot Studio too. Not "which model is smartest?" but "what does one finished task cost?"

Measure the outcome. Then pick the model.
drafts.video_tip: Vertical 10s: two receipts on a desk, one long and one tiny, both stamped 'DONE'. You slide the tiny one forward. Caption: 'Same outcome. Different bill.'

drafts.rides: @OpenAI OpenWorks (1.64M) + @gdb apply now (1.04M) + @gdb OpenWorks intro (205K) + @OpenAIDevs neighborhood shop (60K)
drafts.text:
OpenAI is now funding local AI experts to help small businesses build their own AI tools, at no cost to the business.

The community has been doing this for years. Lunch-and-learns, user groups, "can you look at my flow real quick?"

The hardest part of AI adoption was never the model. It's the person next to you who shows you how.
drafts.video_tip: Vertical 12s: you at a small coffee shop counter pointing at a laptop with the owner, quick cut to them grinning at the result. Caption: 'AI adoption is a people job.'

drafts.rides: @OpenAI Shirudo open-source runtime (2.38M) + GPT-6 Cyber 948 Linux kernel bugs (654K) + @gdb machine speed (137K)
drafts.text:
OpenAI says GPT-6 Cyber helped validate 948 Linux kernel bugs in one run. Patches went to humans for review.

Then they open-sourced Shirudo, a runtime that lets agents shield systems from exploits without downtime.

Agents found the bugs. People reviewed the fixes.

That's the pattern I want for every agent in the enterprise.
drafts.video_tip: Vertical 8s: a screen recording of an approval card popping up, you tap Approve with one finger. Caption: 'Agent finds. Human approves.'

Copilot's new Home splits it nicely:

Chat for the quick stuff.
Cowork for the jobs you'd normally block an afternoon for.

My rule: if I'd explain it in one message, Chat. If I'd explain it in a meeting, Cowork.

Keep calm and hand it off.
